items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: And Gene kind of adopted me as his protégé.

ctx.x: About 40. So anyway Gene brought about six or eight of us up on the stage and I was thrilled to be standing on the bandstand at the Meadowbrook. I had worked there many times after that, but I was like this was big time stuff. So anyway Gene goes down the line, put his hands over this guy and over this guy and over this guy. And I was the last one he came to. And I got the biggest hand. I don’t see how anybody remembered me. And some guys had their own cheering sections there. But still and all, my mother said,…

And I was a lucky kid. I was lucky I met those guys, and had that opportunity to play with them at an early age, and I was a heavy listener and a heavy practicer. And I had some luck. And that was a lucky day for me because I was a little on the sick side, I had a sore throat and a little temperature. They said, “maybe you better stay home.” I said, “no I’m not going to stay home, take me down there.” Because I couldn’t drive. So that was it. And Gene kind of adopted me as his protégé.
